product_brief: Enterprise software platform providing virtualization, storage, and networking with built-in cryptographic security and PQC migration readiness.
pqc_capability_description: VMware Avi Load Balancer supports hybrid post-quantum key exchange in TLS. VCF is preparing for PQC via TLS Profiles, Crypto Bill of Materials (CBOM), and hybrid signing infrastructure. Full support is gated by upstream library FIPS certification and standard finalization.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECDSA, AES, SHA-256, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA
key_management_model: Organization-controlled infrastructure; administrators confirm cryptographic host fingerprints; certificates issued/managed by internal infrastructure; identities verified against owned directories; TPM 2.0 integration for hardware-rooted attestation.
architecture_type: Hybrid TLS key exchange (conventional + PQC); hybrid signing (traditional + post-quantum signatures); FIPS-compliant architecture dependent on upstream cryptographic libraries.
fips_validated: Yes (VCF is FIPS-compliant; PQC algorithms cannot be enabled until FIPS-certified implementations are available; FIPS 206 expected late 2026/early 2027)
primary_platforms: VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware ESXi, VMware vCenter, VMware vSAN
regulatory_status: Aligned with NSA CNSA 2.0 timelines; NIST IR 8547 transition plan; FIPS compliance
pqc_roadmap_details: Commitment to adopt PQC-resistant algorithms per NSA CNSA 2.0 timelines, with full transition required by 2035. NIST deprecates RSA-2048 by 2030 and disallows by 2035. VCF PQC support depends on upstream library updates and FIPS certification.
signature_schemes: Current: RSA, ECDSA. Planned: ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, hybrid signing (traditional + post-quantum)
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Building a Crypto Bill of Materials (CBOM) that maps cryptographic algorithms in use across VCF and identifies areas affected by PQC migration.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: PQC implementation is gated by upstream work; dependencies on cryptographic libraries (OpenSSL, Bouncy Castle) and higher-layer standards; Broadcom participates in standards bodies (TCG, UEFI Forum, Confidential Computing Consortium).
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Migration involves inventorying cryptography across TLS, certificates, HSMs, and code signing; requires coordination between platform, workloads, and external services; hybrid modes recommended for transition.
organizational_readiness: Requires inventory of cryptography, coordination of platform/workloads/external services, and attention to long-lived data; VCF provides TLS Profiles and CBOM to assist.

product_brief: An operating system release featuring updated security tools, PQC support via NSS and OpenSSL, and enhanced SELinux policies.
pqc_capability_description: Oracle Linux 9.7 introduces a PQ subpolicy in crypto-policies enabling post-quantum cryptography. NSS (3.112) supports ML-DSA and hybrid MLKEM1024. OpenSSL (3.5) includes ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA. Hybrid ML-KEM works in FIPS mode. rpm-sequoia supports ML-DSA for RPM signatures.
crypto_primitives: ML-DSA, ML-KEM, SLH-DSA, Ed25519, secp256r1, secp384r1, SHAKE-128, SHAKE-256
fips_validated: Yes (Hybrid ML-KEM works in FIPS mode; fips-provider-next is a technology preview for future validation; openssl-fips-provider remains the validated FIPS provider)
pqc_roadmap_details: DEFAULT, FUTURE, and FIPS policies prioritize hybrid ML-KEM and pure ML-DSA. PQ subpolicy enables ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87, and hybrid groups (mlkem768x25519, secp256r1mlkem768, secp384r1mlkem1024).

product_brief: Enterprise Linux distribution with NSS module achieving CAVP certification for PQC algorithms, advancing toward FIPS 140-3 validation.
pqc_capability_description: NSS module includes NIST-approved PQC algorithms ML-KEM (key exchange) and ML-DSA (digital signatures). Achieved CAVP certification and entered Modules in Process (MIP) list. Code is feature complete and FIPS 140-3 compliant in nss-3.112. OpenSSL PQC support added in 3.5; FIPS validation begins Q3 2026 for RLC 10.2.
license: Open Source (FIPS PQC engineering work publicly available on GitHub)
latest_version: 9.6 (for RLC with NSS 3.112); 10.2 (mentioned for future OpenSSL validation)
fips_validated: No (In Modules in Process (MIP) list; full FIPS 140-3 validation anticipated Q2 2027 for NSS)
regulatory_status: CAVP Certification (NIST); Modules in Process (MIP) list
pqc_roadmap_details: NSS full FIPS 140-3 validation anticipated Q2 2027. OpenSSL FIPS 140-3 validation begins Q3 2026 for RLC 10.2 and mid-2027 for RLC 9.10. Monitoring upstream PQC for Kernel, GnuTLS, and LibGCrypt.
testing_&_validation_methods: CAVP certification from NIST; passed lab testing; entered Modules in Process (MIP) list.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Open source FIPS PQC compliance code available on GitHub; tracking upstream PQC implementation for Kernel, GnuTLS, and LibGCrypt.

product_brief: Hybrid cloud operating system with default post-quantum cryptography support for TLS, SSH, and package signing.
pqc_capability_description: RHEL 10.1 enables PQC by default in TLS and SSH using hybrid ML-KEM key exchange. Supports ML-DSA signatures in OpenSSL, GnuTLS, NSS, and Go. RPM packages are signed with hybrid ML-DSA-87 and Ed448 keys via Sequoia-PGP. PQC was technology preview in RHEL 10.0; generally available in 10.1.
crypto_primitives: RSA, ECDSA (implied by "elliptic curves"), ML-KEM, ML-DSA, Ed448, SHA512, SHA256
key_management_model: Hybrid (Classic + PQC), HSM-backed (via PKCS#11 integration for RPM signing)
target_industries: Enterprise, Government (implied by regulatory mentions like European Cyber Resilience Act)
regulatory_status: Aligns with European Cyber Resilience Act; mentions regulatory requirements for PQC software signing.
pqc_roadmap_details: PQC key exchange and signatures are generally available in RHEL 10.1. More protocols will follow in the future. Go ML-DSA support anticipated in a future release.
testing_&_validation_methods: Product-wide testing effort of PQC key exchange and certificates; issues fixed in upstream/downstream.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Red Hat contributed funding to Sequoia-PGP implementation; uses hybrid signing for packages.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: PQC enabled by default in RHEL 10.1. RHEL 9.7 requires enabling "PQ" policy module. Backward compatibility maintained via hybrid signatures (older systems validate RSA only).
organizational_readiness: Users encouraged to test hybrid PQC key exchange and dual classic/PQC TLS certificate servers.

product_brief: Android 17 OS integrating NIST PQC standards for quantum-resistant boot, attestation, and app signing.
pqc_capability_description: Android 17 integrates NIST PQC standards, specifically ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm). It upgrades Android Verified Boot (AVB) and Remote Attestation (KeyMint) to use PQC. Android Keystore natively supports ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 for hardware-backed signatures. Play App Signing supports hybrid signatures (classical + PQC) for APKs.
crypto_primitives: ML-DSA, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87, classical elliptic curve cryptography (implied by "swapping today's digital locks" and "hybrid" context, though specific classical algos not explicitly named beyond general reference)
key_management_model: Android Keystore (hardware-backed via TEE), Google Cloud KMS (for Play App Signing keys), KeyMint (for attestation certificate chains)
architecture_type: OS-level integration, hardware-backed (TEE/KeyMint), hybrid signing (classical + PQC)
pqc_roadmap_details: Phase 1 (Android 17): Securing foundation (AVB, Attestation), Empowering Developers (Keystore, Play Signing), Ecosystem Scale (Hybrid APK signatures). Future roadmap: Integrate post-quantum key encapsulation into KeyMint, Key Attestation, and Remote Key Provisioning.
signature_schemes: ML-DSA, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87, hybrid signatures (classical + PQC)
